exercise.name: Barbell One Arm Bent over Row

reference.title: Barbell One Arm Bent over Row
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be read from this environment, gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy, so the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Brace in the hinge, breathe out as the bar comes up, in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s down

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 2 s down
prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: the long bar must stay level in the hand, so start with an empty or light bar.
prescription.progression: Add 1.25-2.5 kg per side once the bar stays level and the trunk still for every rep.

cues.text: Feet a little wider than the hips, knees soft, hinge forward with a flat back; left hand braced on the left thigh above the knee. Grip the bar in the middle with the right hand, palm facing in, bar pointing front to back beside the right leg.
Drive the right elbow up and back past the ribs, keeping the bar level.
Squeeze the shoulder blade back for a moment; the trunk does not twist.
Lower slowly to a straight arm, plates clear of the floor.
Keep the hinge and the brace; do all reps, then switch arms.

mistakes.fix: Grip exactly at the middle (the balance point) and squeeze hard; lighter plates help.
Keep the shoulders and hips square to the floor; lighter load.
Drive the elbow back toward the hip.
Press the free hand into the thigh and keep the chest proud.

kinematics.norm: Hinged trunk held still; rows load the low back and trunk muscles (Fenwick 2009)
About 80-100 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Held at its middle, bar level; one-sided loading asks more of the trunk to resist rotation (Saeterbakken 2012)
About 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Clear space in front of and behind you for the long bar.
Start with an empty or lightly loaded bar; a tipping bar strains the wrist.
Low-back pain: use a bench-supported dumbbell row instead.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Grip: shorter bar or a landmine handle.
Lower back: one-arm dumbbell row on a bench.
regressions: One-arm dumbbell row on a bench.
progressions: More plates once the bar stays level.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the elbow back past the trunk.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blade back at the top.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bend the elbow; the neutral grip shares the work with brachialis.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Extends the shoulder behind the trunk.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: With the flexors, stop the long bar tipping in the hand.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the trunk twisting toward the bar (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the trunk twisting toward the bar (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hold the hips in the hinge.
